definitions.explanation: The pouch on the abdomen of marsupials such as kangaroos and koalas, in which newborns continue to develop after birth. Also refers to the brood pouch of seahorses and similar animals.

examples.japanese: カンガルーの{育児嚢|いくじのう}から{赤|あか}ちゃんが{顔|かお}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: A baby peeked out from the kangaroo's pouch.

examples.japanese: {有袋類|ゆうたいるい}は{育児嚢|いくじのう}の{中|なか}で{子|こ}どもを{育|そだ}てる。
examples.english: Marsupials raise their young inside a pouch.

examples.japanese: タツノオトシゴの{雄|おす}は{育児嚢|いくじのう}で{卵|たまご}を{抱|かか}え、{孵化|ふか}するまで{守|まも}る。
examples.english: Male seahorses carry eggs in their brood pouch and protect them until they hatch.

notes:
A zoological term composed of {育児|いくじ} (child-rearing) and {嚢|のう} (sac, pouch). Most commonly associated with kangaroos and other marsupials, but also used for the brood pouch of seahorses and certain crustaceans.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {育児嚢|いくじのう}の{中|なか}: inside the pouch
- {育児嚢|いくじのう}から{出|で}る: to come out of the pouch
- {育児嚢|いくじのう}で{育|そだ}てる: to raise in the pouch

RELATED WORDS:
- {有袋類|ゆうたいるい}: marsupials — animals that have a pouch
- {袋|ふくろ}: pouch, bag — the informal way to refer to a marsupial's pouch
